subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: Should OpenClaw accept the patched-Codex runtime prerequisite and policy-active unified-exec/fresh-thread behavior after the missing `code_mode_exec` normalization is fixed?
rationale: The PR changes tool-execution enforcement and session binding behavior; automation can repair the missing alias, but only maintainers can decide whether this runtime prerequisite and compatibility tradeoff is acceptable for policy-active Codex users.

options.title: Repair then review security tradeoff
options.body: Add the `code_mode_exec` normalization and tests first, then keep the PR draft or human-gated until maintainers explicitly accept the Codex runtime and compatibility implications.

options.title: Pause behind packaged Codex proof
options.body: Keep this draft paused until OpenClaw pins or otherwise proves a Codex package that emits the required Code Mode PreToolUse event without local binary patch assumptions.

options.title: Prefer fail-closed mitigation
options.body: Use the adjacent fail-closed or broader native-surface mitigation path instead if maintainers do not want to rely on positive delivery through unified exec yet.

recommendation.title: Repair then review security tradeoff
recommendation.body: Add the `code_mode_exec` normalization and tests first, then keep the PR draft or human-gated until maintainers explicitly accept the Codex runtime and compatibility implications.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the best available likely decision owner from recent native hook fallback work and is better positioned than automation to accept or reject the security/compatibility tradeoff.
